messages:
sam: Quick design review — putting the Filters + Actions layout for Prompt Evals up for feedback. Screenshot: https://files.redwood/s/xyz. Main asks: microcopy for bulk actions, keyboard/focus order, and whether Approve should live in the overflow or be a primary CTA. Need decisions before next dev sprint. elaine: Skimming the mock — love the compact filter row. Two immediate UX nits: (1) 'Approve' in overflow feels discoverability-poor when users select items. (2) The disabled CTA copy currently reads 'Approve' (disabled) — should be 'Select results to approve' so intent is clearer. jon: Agree with discoverability note. From infra perspective moving Approve out of overflow is fine but adds a sticky action bar when selections > 0. Implementation cost is minor, but we should avoid frequent layout shifts. Proposal: keep a compact floating bar that appears anchored to the bottom of the list when selection count > 0. jon: quick aria/markup example for floating bar focus handling: ```html
Selected 3
``` This keeps screen readers informed when the bar appears. aria: A11y notes: - Keyboard order must be: filter pills -> list items -> action bar. Currently mock puts actions before the list in DOM order which breaks tab flow. - Use clear labels: 'Approve selected results' is clearer than 'Bulk approve'. Avoid abbreviations. - When approval completes, announce via aria-live="assertive" toast: '3 results approved'. - Color contrast: the disabled state for the CTA falls below 4.5:1 on small text. Need stronger contrast or larger text. elaine: Good catches @aria. Two questions for product/eng: (A) copy preference — 'Approve 3' vs 'Approve selected results' (conciseness vs clarity)? (B) should the floating bar include a count chip or rely on the text only? My instinct: label + count chip (makes the action weightier). sam: My lean: prefer clarity for first pass — 'Approve selected results' + count chip. We can shorten later if metrics show users find it verbose. Action placement: move Approve out of overflow into the floating/sticky action bar. Requirements summary for handoff: - CTA text: 'Approve selected results' - When none selected: CTA disabled and label changed to 'Select results to approve' - Floating/sticky action bar appears on selection with a visible focus ring and first tabbable element = count chip then Approve button - Toast uses aria-live="assertive" and says '{n} results approved' elaine: I'll update mocks with the floating bar, count chip, and focus outline spec. Will also adjust disabled color to meet 4.5:1. ETA EOD for updated screens. jon: I'll spike the floating bar behavior in a small branch and verify there are no jank layout shifts. Will also wire the aria-live snippet. Assigning self to feasibility check — ETA tomorrow morning. aria: I'll write a short a11y checklist (keyboard flow, aria-live tests, contrast checks) and review the updated mock when ready. uploader-bot: uploaded 2 files: filters_actions_v2.png, floating_bar_spec.sketch (https://files.redwood/s/xyz) sam: Thanks everyone — follow-ups: @elaine update mocks, @jon feasibility spike, @aria a11y checklist. If any of you see big issues in the spike, flag before the sprint planning meeting tomorrow. :thumbsup:
